claims.text: Distinguish swimmer's ear from other causes, including middle-ear disease; need exam
claims.quote: clinicians should distinguish diffuse AOE from other causes of otalgia, otorrhea, and inflammation of the external ear canal

claims.text: Topical therapy is initial treatment for uncomplicated AOE
claims.quote: clinicians should prescribe topical preparations for initial therapy of diffuse, uncomplicated AOE

claims.text: No routine systemic antibiotics unless extension outside canal or host factors
claims.quote: clinicians should not prescribe systemic antimicrobials as initial therapy for diffuse, uncomplicated AOE unless there is extension outside the ear canal or the presence of specific host factors

claims.text: Assess and treat pain
claims.quote: clinicians should assess patients with AOE for pain and recommend analgesic treatment based on the severity of pain

claims.text: Non-ototoxic drop when perforation known or suspected, including tube
claims.quote: clinicians should prescribe a non-ototoxic preparation when the patient has a known or suspected perforation of the tympanic membrane, including a tympanostomy tube

claims.text: Reassess if no response in 48 to 72 hours
claims.quote: clinicians should reassess the patient who fails to respond to the initial therapeutic option within 48 to 72 hours [corrected] to confirm the diagnosis of diffuse AOE and to exclude other causes of illness

claims.text: Obstructed canal: clinician aural toilet and/or wick; teach drop administration
claims.quote: enhance the delivery of topical drops by informing the patient how to administer topical drops and by performing aural toilet, placing a wick, or both, when the ear canal is obstructed

claims.text: Diabetes, immunocompromised state, prior radiotherapy, nonintact TM, tubes modify management
claims.quote: assess the patient with diffuse AOE for factors that modify management (nonintact tympanic membrane, tympanostomy tube, diabetes, immunocompromised state, prior radiotherapy)

claims.text: AOE is diffuse inflammation of the canal, almost exclusively bacterial (contagious section)
claims.quote: recommendations for management will be limited to diffuse AOE, which is almost exclusively a bacterial infection

claims.text: Topical antibiotics and analgesics are mainstays; oral antibiotics only for spread beyond canal or host factors
claims.quote: Oral antibiotics are indicated only if evidence of cellulitis occurs outside of the ear canal or if associated conditions such as immunocompromise, diabetes mellitus, or conditions that would not allow for the use of topical treatment are found.

claims.text: No preparation clinically superior; choice by cost, TM integrity, adherence
claims.quote: There is no evidence that any one preparation is clinically superior to another, and the choice of treatment is based on factors such as cost, whether the tympanic membrane is intact, and patient adherence.

claims.text: Tragus/pinna tenderness classic; redness and swelling of canal
claims.quote: Tenderness on movement of the pinna or tragus is the classic finding.

claims.text: Symptoms: itching, fullness, hearing change, discharge
claims.quote: Itching ... Sense of fullness ... With or without hearing loss or jaw pain ... May also have otorrhea, tympanic membrane rupture, pinna cellulitis, or local lymphadenitis

claims.text: Risk factors: hearing aids, earbuds, earplugs, instrumentation, eczema, swimming most common
claims.quote: Swimming is the most common risk factor for acute otitis externa. ... Hearing aid or ear bud usage ... Earplug usage ... Instrumentation or itching of canal ... Eczema

claims.text: AOM: middle-ear effusion, no tragal or pinnal tenderness; treated with systemic antibiotics (different plan)
claims.quote: Presence of middle ear effusion, no tragal or pinnal tenderness ... Use pneumatic otoscopy or tympanometry; treat with systemic antibiotics

claims.text: Ototoxic agents (aminoglycosides, isopropyl alcohol) not used with perforation; neomycin product warning
claims.quote: If a perforation or suspected perforation of the tympanic membrane has occurred, topical medications that are potentially ototoxic (e.g., aminoglycosides, isopropyl alcohol) should not be used

claims.text: Ofloxacin and cipro/dex usable with perforated TM; quinolones only FDA-approved for middle ear
claims.quote: The only topical agents approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the middle ear are quinolones.

claims.text: Wick for marked canal edema
claims.quote: If marked canal edema has occurred, the physician may use a wick to improve drug delivery to the canal.

claims.text: Analgesics: acetaminophen, NSAIDs
claims.quote: Analgesics that can provide relief include acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

claims.text: Most patients improve within 24 to 72 hours; reassess if not
claims.quote: Most patients will improve within 24 to 72 hours of beginning treatment. For those who do not improve in that time frame, reassessment is warranted.

claims.text: Follow-up if symptoms not resolved after two weeks
claims.quote: Follow-up should be recommended for any patient who does not have symptom resolution after two weeks of therapy.

claims.text: Specialist referral if condition worsens despite adequate therapy
claims.quote: if the patient's condition worsens despite adequate therapy

claims.text: Facial numbness or paralysis with ear pain fits Ramsay Hunt syndrome, treated with antivirals and systemic corticosteroids
claims.quote: Herpetic ulcers in canal; may have facial numbness or paralysis, severe pain, loss of taste ... Treatment includes antivirals, systemic corticosteroids

claims.text: Prevention: avoid canal injury, keep canal dry; poorly fitting earplugs raise risk
claims.quote: Keys to prevention include avoiding injury to the ear canal and keeping it free of water.

claims.text: Video visit cannot replace otoscopy: pneumatic otoscopy differentiates AOE from otitis media
claims.quote: Use of pneumatic otoscopy is recommended to help differentiate acute otitis externa from otitis media

claims.text: No drying drops with tubes, punctured eardrum, swimmer's ear, or drainage
claims.quote: Don't use these drops if you have ear tubes (tympanostomy tubes), punctured ear drums, swimmer's ear, or ear drainage.

claims.text: Ask a clinician about preventive drying drops; see clinician for ear pain or drainage
claims.quote: Check with your healthcare provider about using ear-drying drops after swimming ... Check with your healthcare provider if you have ear pain or drainage from the ear.

claims.text: Prevention: towel dry, tilt head to drain, no objects including cotton swabs
claims.quote: Tilt head back and forth so that each ear faces down to allow water to drain out of the ear canal. ... Use a towel to dry ears well. ... Including cotton-tip swabs, pencils, paperclips, or keys.

claims.text: Swimmer's ear is not contagious
claims.quote: Swimmer's ear cannot be spread from one person to another.

claims.quote: Ten drops (0.5 mL, 1.5 mg ofloxacin) instilled into the affected ear once daily for seven days.

claims.text: Different twice-daily middle-ear regimens; indications involving non-intact membrane
claims.quote: Ten drops (0.5 mL, 1.5 mg ofloxacin) instilled into the affected ear twice daily for fourteen days.

claims.text: Warm bottle in hand one or two minutes
claims.quote: The solution should be warmed by holding the bottle in the hand for one or two minutes.

claims.text: Pull outer ear up and back for canal infection; avoid tip contamination; wash hands

claims.text: Remain in position five minutes

claims.text: Avoid swimming unless doctor instructs otherwise
claims.quote: Avoid swimming unless the doctor has instructed otherwise.

claims.text: AOE: 4 drops twice daily for 7 days

claims.text: 19 RCTs, 3,382 participants; only two in primary care; low quality

claims.text: No clinically meaningful differences among most topical treatments; steroid not proven necessary

claims.text: Topical treatment alone effective; choice by ototoxicity, contact sensitivity, cost, dosing

claims.text: Drop choice factors include contact sensitivity (allergy), cost, dosing schedule

claims.text: Symptoms persisting beyond two weeks are treatment failures
